title: Student t errors gave no clear monthly PDO probability forecast gain in 1981-2025
abstract: We tested Student t errors against Gaussian errors for one-month Pacific Decadal Oscillation probability forecasts. Both models used the same mean with season, recent PDO, recent Nino 3.4 and annual PDO memory. Each year used only earlier target months for fits. In 540 test months in 1981-2025, learned Student t errors gave a mean log score gain of -0.000499 nats per month. The conditional 95% three-year block interval was -0.001120 to +0.000221. All 45 expanding fits reached the allowed limit of 100 degrees of freedom, close to Gaussian. A fixed five-degree model lost 0.022516 nats per month, with limits of -0.030688 to -0.014279. Its 90% interval score was slightly better, so the loss did not hold for every metric. Rolling training gave no clear density score gain. The primary test gives no clear benefit from heavy tails. Revised data, the finite tail limit, one mean model and conditional uncertainty limit inference. This is a method benchmark, not a physical cause test. Code, provenance, aggregate scores, numerical checks and a figure are included. Source tables and monthly records remain external.

display.caption: Student t minus Gaussian log score gains. Positive values mean better forecasts. Lines show separate conditional 95% three-year block intervals.
